citations.quote: Kahneman and Tversky describe the representativeness heuristic as our tendency to judge likelihood by similarity.
The conjunction fallacy refers to the mistake of judging an event A ∩ B to be more likely than either A or B alone.
Base rate neglect refers to the tendency for individuals to react too strongly to information

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Kahneman-Tversky's representativeness heuristic judges likelihood by similarity, and accounts for two robust errors -- the conjunction fallacy (Linda) and base-rate neglect (overreaction to a positive medical test) -- the psychology Gennaioli-Shleifer formalize.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Representativeness, Conjunction Fallacy, Base-Rate Neglect
